analysis.investment_thesis: A micro-cap (INR 90 Cr) SME-style IT outfit with only ~3 years of reported earnings and a P/B near 3x fails virtually every Graham filter. The tiny INR 9 Cr revenue base and negative free cash flow offer no margin of safety at INR 77.
key_strengths: Zero borrowings — clean balance sheet with INR 31 Cr equity
Operating cash flow positive in all 3 reported years
key_risks: Tiny revenue base (INR 9 Cr) — no proven earning power over a business cycle
P/B ~2.9x and P/E 18.6 — no margin of safety
Negative FCF (-2 Cr in 2025) despite IPO cash inflow; equity jumped from 10→31 Cr via dilution
red_flags: Recent IPO / SME-scale listing lacking 5+ year earnings record
Reserves volatile (5→3→21) suggesting capital restructuring around listing
Price well above Graham Number (sqrt(22.5 × ~2.5 EPS × ~26 BVPS) ≈ 38, vs market price 77)
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my vantage point, Identixweb is precisely the kind of security The Intelligent Investor warns against: a freshly-listed, micro-cap technology promoter floated at a price the underwriters — not the buyer — set. Only three years of data exist, revenue is a trivial INR 9 Cr, and the equity base tripled from INR 10 Cr to INR 31 Cr in a single year, which tells me the 2025 "book value" largely reflects fresh IPO proceeds rather than accumulated earning power. At INR 77 the stock trades at roughly 2.9x book and ~30x FY25 earnings on my adjusted view — nowhere near my requirement of P/E <15 and P/B <1.5.

The business has redeeming features: no debt, positive operating cash flow three years running, and ostensibly strong ROCE. But ROE inflated by a thin asset base is not the same as durable earning power, and FCF has been negative in 2024 and 2025. The Graham Number is roughly INR 38 versus a market price of INR 77 — a 100% premium to intrinsic value, not a discount. There is no dividend history, no 5-year earnings record, and no margin of safety. Mr. Market is offering me enthusiasm, not a bargain. Avoid.
